newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended lower, pressured by weakness in U.S. Treasuries and German Bunds.

The Swiss short end was also undermined by what appeared to be a successful outlook for a single European currency after a European Union summit in Amsterdam. This led to reduced safe-haven demand for short-term Swiss franc holdings.

U.S. Treasuries were lower after release of latest U.S. economic data. Some of the data appeared to favour bonds, including news May housing starts fell 4.8 percent in May, while the U.S. May consumer price index rose by only 0.1 percent overall and by 0.2 percent in the core rate.

Treasuries fell further later in the day after news U.S. May capacity use was at its highest level since September 1995, and industrial output rose 0.4 percent. Real earnings also rose 0.3 percent in May. German Bunds meanwhile fell below support.
One trader described selling mainly as profit-taking.
At the same time, he said that buyers were seen at lower levels which helped to put a floor under Swiss bond prices.
Swiss prices for short-term paper also fell. One trader said prices fell on reversal of safe-haven holdings in Swiss franc following the summit in Amsterdam.
Comi medium-term bond COMIc1 settles down two at 113.48
Euro Swiss francs FESc1 down eight at 98.46.
